key_insight: Co-PiLOT turns inverse design into a constrained search in a learned latent space, using a decoder as a validity prior and physics-informed optimization to efficiently target desired material behavior.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical workflow for designing magnesium alloy microstructures and textures with expensive simulators, reducing trial-and-error in computational materials engineering.
method: Train a ViT-based encoder with latent diffusion / diffusion-transformer / rectified-flow decoders on ~80,000 EBSD microstructure samples.
Use the decoder as a learned feasibility filter and convert latent candidates through a self-segmenting orientation codec for crystal plasticity simulation.
Optimize latent variables with MERIDIAN: deep-kernel GP uncertainty, failure-aware feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition.
evidence_signal: On a budget of 160 simulations, the best ViT-FMDiT + MERIDIAN setup achieved the strongest target-driven objective and cut relative target error by 3–22% versus seven baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the learned latent representation and decoder fidelity, so out-of-distribution microstructures or weak feasibility prediction could still mislead the optimizer.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
